races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Now Maiden Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Firebrand
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with solid good-ground form (four placings from 11 similar-going runs), handles this trip and track profile well under Daniel King, and Nallen's yard has a respectable 14-day strike rate; six-year-old with experience but yet to win.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Ciaran Murphy racing prominently, only one run at this trip and limited good-ground experience (3 from 15 similar-going), but fresh off 13-day turnaround and bumper winner at 12f suggesting stamina for 2m is not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent prominently-raced type with six placings from 11 good-ground runs at varying distances up to 20f, and a 5-pound claimer on board; the unbeaten record of placing rather than winning is the concern, but the profile fits this shape ideally.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained five-year-old wearing a tongue-strap, racing prominently over a trip and going he handles (9 from 10 similar-going), and a low 14-day yard strike rate shouldn't distract from the strong positional profile suiting this race shape.

runners_data.name: Geashill Poet
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed five-year-old for Adrian Murray wearing a hood; no form data available, unknown style flagged, and trainer has sent just one runner in the last 14 days — total unknown quantity in every respect.

runners_data.name: Man Down
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a tendency to fade in the finish and only one comparable good-ground run to reference; the unknown style tag and finishing pattern are both red flags, and Duggan's two-runner 14-day record offers little confidence.

runners_data.name: Midfield Magic
runners_data.note: Cromwell's runner is the race's confirmed pace-setter and the key shape determinant, but after 151 days off and only one career run on soft ground, fitness and jumping accuracy over a sharp 2m track on good ground are genuine unknowns — the STYLE_FIT tag correctly tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Scotty Joe
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for P J Rothwell returning after 89 days, with a 17th on good ground in his only comparable run — the positional style is honest but the Kilbeggan 2m circuit offers limited room to reel in a sustainable gallop from well back.

runners_data.name: Tomthescaffolder
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's six-year-old wears a tongue-strap, sits off the pace, and has a respectable one placing from five similar-going runs; Darragh O'Keeffe is a strong booking but the hold-up style on this sharp, turning track is a positional disadvantage here.

runners_data.name: Blue Johnl
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a tendency to fade in the finish, mapping as unknown style with two good-ground starts both resulting in mid-pack finishes around 19f trips — the fading pattern and lightly raced tag combine to make this a difficult profile to trust.

runners_data.name: Down After Dark
runners_data.note: Curling's four-year-old has only one run to reference (a pulled-up on good ground over 17f) and wears a hood; the very short six-day turnaround after that debut experience is notable, and lightly raced caution applies in full.

runners_data.name: Power Of Knowledge
runners_data.note: Mullins's four-year-old is the most intriguing unknown — a fifth on debut at 16f on good ground, now stepped to 2m with Mark Walsh riding; the yard's class is the X-factor, but lightly raced caution limits how far up the order this profile can be rated.

runners_data.name: Bayswater Bloom
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for McCutcheon who has finished no better than fifth across four good-ground runs at this type of trip; lightest-weighted runner in the field at 151lbs but the consistent inability to land a blow from the rear makes the profile hard to back.

races.paceDynamic: Midfield Magic is the one confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner maiden hurdle, and with only Firebrand, Baila Conmigo, Whats New, and First Ascent as genuine prominent types behind, the early pace should be controlled and sustainable rather than frantic. Midfield Magic's 151-day layoff is a notable unknown, but nothing in this field appears inclined to pressure them hard from the outset, meaning the leader can dictate comfortably through the early stages on good ground. The hold-up brigade — Scotty Joe, Tomthescaffolder, and Bayswater Bloom — will be tracking a steady gallop from the rear, which on a turning, sharp track like Kilbeggan may leave them with too much ground to make up when the race quickens after the last. This shape — a measured, uncontested lead over 2m on good ground — most favours horses racing prominently who can track the pace without over-exerting, then sustain their effort over the final two flights; prominent closers with tactical speed hold the edge over pure hold-up types here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Midfield Magic dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent runners track efficiently throughout.
scenarios.body: Midfield Magic sets a manageable tempo, allowing Firebrand, Whats New, and First Ascent to travel smoothly in their wake before unleashing their challenge from the second-last; on good ground over 2m at Kilbeggan the winner rarely comes from far back, suiting those who save ground close to the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Midfield Magic's fitness holds after 151 days off and the prominent challengers fail to quicken sufficiently at the business end.
scenarios.body: Cromwell's runner sets a tempo that proves just strong enough to expose the limitations of the pack, and the good ground and flat Kilbeggan finish allow the leader to sustain its effort when rivals expect a collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough and the prominent horses burn out, creating a gap for hold-up types to close.
scenarios.body: Scotty Joe or Tomthescaffolder would need to be produced with a well-timed challenge from the rear to exploit a messy or faster-than-expected gallop, but the compact 2m circuit at Kilbeggan limits the ground they can make up in the final stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed, unknown-style runners — Power Of Knowledge, Down After Dark, or Geashill Poet — shows significantly more than their limited form suggests.
scenarios.body: Mullins's Power Of Knowledge or the Curling-trained Down After Dark could be sitting on a major step forward on debut or near-debut, and if that is the case their tactical position matters less than raw ability; however, the absence of form data makes this a low-probability swing.

watchPoints.text: Midfield Magic's jumping on the first circuit is the race's pivotal moment — if Cromwell's horse is rusty after 151 days and loses the lead early, the entire pace scenario collapses and holds-up could get an unearned run at it.

Watch Whats New at the start and over the early hurdles — the form string includes a U (unseated) and an R (refused), and if the horse loses concentration early the race shape could fragment with no clean leader taking over.

Firebrand, Baila Conmigo, and First Ascent are all prominent types tracking Midfield Magic; if any two of them decide to challenge before the final bend it could turn a sustainable gallop into a contested pace and blow the field apart from the front.

Scotty Joe's 89-day absence and Tomthescaffolder's 27-day gap both merit monitoring in the paddock — if either look below peak fitness, their already-difficult hold-up task on this sharp circuit becomes even more unlikely to produce a challenge.

Power Of Knowledge (Mullins/Mark Walsh) is the most significant lightly raced unknown in the field — if they show any early movement toward a prominent position that contradicts their unknown-style tag, upgrade their chance significantly in any scenario.

races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Now Maiden Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Bud Fox
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on good ground and has three places from five runs at similar going; Cromwell's stable is firing at 4/39 in 14 days and Donoghue is a competent pilot — this prominent-style runner is ideally positioned to sit just off a contested pace and strike late.

runners_data.name: Combs
runners_data.note: Front-runner wearing a tongue-tie returning after 150 days for Elliott; has placed on good ground and carries the strong trainer angle, though the T14 rate of 1/41 is modest — likely to force the pace from the off and could be vulnerable to a fresher rival if the gallop is taxing.

runners_data.name: Goeasyonme
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (just one run, a second over 16f on soft) and an unknown quantity on good ground; Ryan's 0/18 recent strike rate is cold, but the style is unclassified and the unexposed profile warrants respect if the pace suits a midfield move.

runners_data.name: Jack Spriggins
runners_data.note: 748 days off the track and all prior form came in flat or bumper company; the hold-up profile and complete absence of hurdle form makes this a very speculative proposition despite the booking of Kevin Healy.

runners_data.name: Joly Saphir
runners_data.note: One run over hurdles (eighth of field on good, 20f) and a flag for fading in the finish — the hold-up profile and stamina question over 2m on good ground combine to make this hard to assess positively; Fenton's 0/2 recent rate adds little.

runners_data.name: Texas Red
runners_data.note: Active front-runner returning quickly (24 days) with six runs over the course and distance trip, wearing a hood; Rothwell's T14 of 4/21 is respectable and Texas Red has placed once at this level on similar going — likely to push Combs early and could nick it if Combs fires first.

runners_data.name: Unfortunatecharlie
runners_data.note: Unclassified style with an unknown going tag; form figures of 2-1 over hurdles suggest ability but the 124-day layoff and Kelly's 1/18 recent rate add uncertainty — could be better than the market suggests if the going suits.

runners_data.name: Lucky Signal
runners_data.note: Two runs over hurdles (an eighth and a pulled-up), both accompanied by the fading flag; Elliott's yard is the connection of note but this horse has shown nothing to suggest it can cope with a hot pace, and the hold-up style leaves it dependent on a slow run race.

runners_data.name: Mydreamtell
runners_data.note: Two hurdle runs both yielding modest finishes (eighth and sixth on good ground); lightly raced and unclassified in style, with an amateur claim in the saddle and a cold trainer (0/0 T14) — needs significant improvement on shown form.

runners_data.name: Telegram Sam
runners_data.note: Placed fourth on sole hurdle start on good ground (16f) which is genuinely encouraging; Murray's 0/1 T14 is quiet but the unclassified style and 101-day gap mean the true ceiling is unknown — the good-ground experience is a positive hook.

runners_data.name: Inver Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose last two runs produced fifths on good ground at this trip — however, this horse's natural closer style is pushed into midfield on the map by field congestion, meaning it is likely racing out of its ideal position; the fading flag and 0W0P record at similar going temper expectations further.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Jolene
runners_data.note: Two hurdle runs at this trip on good ground yielding sevenths and eighths; the hold-up profile has not paid dividends yet and the 89-day break plus cold trainer (0/1 T14) give little reason to upgrade the form, though 151lbs is one of the lighter weights.

runners_data.name: Asthelightdeclines
runners_data.note: Cromwell has decent stats but this horse began its career with a bolter (B) and two sevenths; its true preference is to race from the rear, though the crowded hold-up division in this field pushes it onto the map in a midfield slot it may not naturally occupy — discount its chance in a scenario that requires a clean hold-up run.

runners_data.name: Cahir Bay
runners_data.note: Flat-bred background with disappointing hurdle debut (14th of field, good ground); the natural hold-up inclination is boxed out by the sheer number of closers in this field, and without a prior hurdle win or place, the burden of proof is firmly on this runner to show improved form.

races.paceDynamic: Combs (tongue-tie, Gordon Elliott) and Texas Red are the two confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field, and both are likely to press forward from the outset, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over 2m on good ground at Kilbeggan. Texas Red has recent course form and is fresh off a 24-day break, while Combs returns after 150 days but has Elliott's strong recent strike rate behind it; neither is likely to yield to the other, meaning the pace should be honest rather than suicidal but competitive enough to stretch the field. Bud Fox is the most natural prominent type capable of tracking close to the pace without burning fuel, and his simlar-going record (3 from 5 at this level) gives him a solid platform if the pace is well-regulated. This race shape — two front-runners pressing each other at an honest clip — tilts the advantage toward a genuine prominent racer who can sit just off the lead and pick up the pieces late, rather than true hold-up horses who will struggle to land a telling blow. Three horses — Inver Bay, Asthelightdeclines, and Cahir Bay — are natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because this field carries more closer/hold-up profiles than the rear positions can accommodate, and none of those three is likely to secure their preferred ground position in a race this size and shape; Combs and Texas Red are best-placed to control the narrative from the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Combs and Texas Red press each other throughout, setting an honest clip that stretches the field and leaves true hold-up horses struggling to close.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners fight it out, burning each other's stamina reserves, leaving a well-positioned prominent runner to sweep past in the closing stages; on 2m good ground at Kilbeggan, a horse racing second or third and jumping well is ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners (most likely Combs) breaks smartly and dictates a controlled pace, the other failing to match strides early.
scenarios.body: With Texas Red unable to match Combs's early stride, Combs can dictate from the front at a pace that suits, rationing energy for the run-in; Elliott's 1/41 recent strike rate is modest but Combs has finishing positions of 3-3 on similar good ground and has course-distance experience to call on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfielders Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners burn each other out badly enough that the pace proves genuinely strong, allowing a well-covered midfield runner to sprint clear in the final flight.
scenarios.body: A horse settled mid-division in the slipstream of a truly run race can motor home in the final half-mile when the leaders hit a wall; Goeasyonme (showed a clear second on debut), Telegram Sam, and Unfortunatecharlie are unknown quantities whose form figures leave improvement entirely plausible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart in a scramble, pace collapses, and genuine hold-up runners get an unusually clean run through the field from their natural rearward position.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses like Inver Bay, Asthelightdeclines, and Cahir Bay — all redistributed out of their natural hold-up position due to field congestion — actually managing to find daylight from the rear, which is structurally unlikely in a 14-runner field with active front-runners; the probability is suppressed accordingly.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Texas Red or Combs flinches at the start — if either breaks slowly, the other could steal an uncontested lead and completely alter the pace dynamic, potentially making this a front-runner's race rather than a battle.
Bud Fox is 117 days off the track and ran a flat fifth last time; if Cromwell's stable runner is in any way ring-rusty, the prominent pitch that suits him becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Inver Bay, Asthelightdeclines, and Cahir Bay are all true hold-up types squeezed into the midfield zone by a field full of closers — in a 14-runner race with active front-runners, watch for all three to be caught wide or without a clear run late.

Goeasyonme is unbeaten in style terms (second from one start) but carries the lightly-raced flag and an unknown going profile beyond soft ground — watch its market moves before the off as a potential dark horse from the unclassified group.
Jack Spriggins reappears after 748 days off — watch the pre-race market and parade ring closely, as any significant drifting would confirm this is a fitness run rather than a winning mission.

races.name: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction & Median Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Coral Reid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Tom Kelly (7lb claimer) and E McNamara; sole form figure is a remote seventh on Soft — needs a stronger pace than Rokanako is likely to set to get involved from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Eternal Reward
runners_data.note: Pulls up or finishes tailed off in hurdle runs on Good, carries a documented fades-in-finish flag, and Danny Mullins cannot mask a horse whose jumping confidence looks fragile — the 36-day break does little to address those concerns.

runners_data.name: It's All Clear
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer with four top-four finishes on Good, always prominent under Ryan Treacy; the tongue-tie is retained, the 2m3f trip suits her staying profile, and she represents the most reliably placed runner in the field on these conditions.

runners_data.name: Rokanako
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who sets the tactical agenda here; his STYLE_FIT tag acknowledges he is technically listed as Prominent rather than Lead, but he is functionally the race's pace-setter and his one win came on Good ground — the concern is whether he can withstand challengers over the final two hurdles after controlling throughout.

runners_data.name: Splendid Fellow
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's prominent-style five-year-old returns after 115 days off but has course-and-distance placed form on Good; Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride and the step back up to 2m3f after a 2m flat run last time looks like a positive switch for this stayer.

runners_data.name: Bigcitydreams
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unknown quantity returns from 334 days off with only a pulled-up hurdle run to his name; the yard's 14-day strike rate is respectable, but the lengthy absence and minimal form evidence make his true level impossible to assess — treat as a significant wildcard.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Solid flat form on Good but consistently finishing fifth or sixth; a true hold-up performer whose mapping to midfield reflects field congestion at the rear rather than any change in racing style — the STYLE_FIT discount is real, and his OR of 95 makes the task steep against 120-rated rivals.

runners_data.name: La Muleta
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single debut second and 118 days since; P J Rothwell's yard has been active and Kevin Healy's 7lb claim helps, but the form base is almost non-existent — if the extra distance and a hurdling education since debut have clicked, she could outrun a big price.

races.paceDynamic: Rokanako is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no obvious challenger likely to press hard from the outset over 2m3f on Good ground at Kilbeggan, he is set to control matters from the front at a sustainable, measured gallop. Splendid Fellow and It's All Clear are both prominent-style types who will want to race close to the pace, and their presence means Rokanako will not be entirely alone up front, but neither is likely to launch a serious early battle for the lead. Western Shores is a genuine hold-up performer in style but, with the rear of the field already occupied by Coral Reid, Eternal Reward, and others, he is mapped to midfield — a position that is not his natural home and from which his STYLE_FIT discount applies. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter setting a comfortable tempo — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can travel within striking range and pick off a tiring leader in the final half-mile, rather than true hold-up horses who need a fast, strung-out gallop to manufacture late momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rokanako Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Rokanako dictates an uncontested lead and the race is run at a steady-to-fair clip throughout.
scenarios.body: Rokanako sets the fractions to suit himself, but horses who have been travelling prominently or in close midfield — conserving energy behind him — are ideally placed to challenge from the second-last hurdle; the Good ground and 2m3f trip rewards those who have been economical early and finish with purpose.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Gallop, Strong Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and a well-held horse produces a single sustained run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow race can compress the field, but a horse with a clean jump and the stamina to sustain a run from off the pace — rather than a sprint finish — will catch the prominent horses flat-footed late; Eternal Reward's similar-going form gives minimal encouragement, but La Muleta's unknown profile gives her a wildcard profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Rokanako Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Rokanako's front-running effort proves so well-judged that no rival can close the gap at the business end.
scenarios.body: On a Good surface over a galloping 2m3f circuit, a pace-setter who has stolen an uncontested lead and conserved energy jumping well can simply outgrind late challengers; Rokanako's single win came over this trip profile and his STYLE_FIT tag relates to position, not suitability to leading — he is doing what he naturally wants to do here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Runners Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced, form-unknown runners — Bigcitydreams or La Muleta — produces a performance well above their limited exposed profile.
scenarios.body: Bigcitydreams returns from 334 days off for Gordon Elliott and carries the unknown-quantity tag that can be dangerous in maiden company; La Muleta showed ability on debut and the longer trip may be the key that unlocks improvement — either could upset the established order if class and freshness combine.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rokanako's jumping under Phillip Enright — if he meets a hurdle wrong early and loses his lead before the halfway point, the entire race shape collapses and the prominent challengers inherit a scrappier, more unpredictable contest.

Bigcitydreams is 334 days absent for Gordon Elliott; the stable's ability to produce fit, forward-going horses fresh means this runner should not be ignored on fitness grounds, but a reproduction of the pulled-up run would derail any scenario he features in.

Eternal Reward's fade flag combined with a documented history of pulling up on Good ground (16th of 16) means Danny Mullins may be steering a horse who needs heavy or soft conditions to fire — monitor behaviour in the parade ring and early in the race.

La Muleta's unknown profile at 2m3f and the yard's recent 4/21 14-day form makes her a price worth tracking — if she is backed in the market before the off, it would carry meaningful significance given how little public form she has shown.

Western Shores' redistribution from hold-up to midfield means punters should note that his mapping overstates his likely tactical aggressiveness — if he drifts back to his natural rear position early, he will need a stronger gallop than Rokanako is forecast to set to reach the principals late.

races.name: Midland Breeders Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Tir Og
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with good-ground form (placed at 2W4P on sim going), returning from 81 days off for Seymour; will battle for the lead with Ivana D'alco and how she handles that duel over 2m3f on good ground is the central question for her chance.

runners_data.name: Ivana D'alco
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained, Brian Hayes in the saddle — a high-profile booking — and her only two runs on good ground produced a win and a sixth; wearing a hood and returning after 28 days, she is the most likely candidate to convert front-running advantage into a result.
runners_data.comment: Ivana D'alco returns on familiar going after a 28-day break, and her two wins in her last five starts — including a victory last time out — give her real claims, though a fall in recent form and a mark of 108 leave questions unanswered.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Has a genuine fade-in-finish flag that is a concern in a genuinely run 2m3f; returned just six days ago and the quick turnaround for Collins' yard (0/2 in 14 days) adds doubt, though her two career wins have both come on good ground at 16-18f.
runners_data.comment: Small Bucks won two starts back but finished eighth last time out, and a six-day turnaround on today's going leaves freshness in question; the 164 lb burden will ask plenty of a mare ranked mid-division on ratings.

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Good-ground specialist who has won twice on it at 16f, but a fade-in-finish flag and the step up to 2m3f (longest trip in her recent hist) are the key tests; Keith Donoghue takes over from previous connections and the tongue-tie is retained.
runners_data.comment: Del Boys Diva won two of her last five starts, with back-to-back victories two and three runs back giving her solid recent claims, but she was fifth last time out and our rating of 97 leaves her with ground to make up on the top-rated runners.

runners_data.name: Shirzan
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for P G Fahey with only one win on good ground so far (at 16f on soft/yielding); stepping up in trip to 2m3f for the first time over hurdles, which is a question mark, and the 7lb claimer Cullinan rides for the first time.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below her official mark on our figures and ranked near the foot of the field, Shirzan is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and the fact she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Placed 2/18f on good ground last time out and handles this distance well (consistent 19-20f history); tongue-tie and pad retained, Flanagan in the saddle for Hassett who is 1/5 in the last 14 days — steady enough profile to be a quiet threat from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Tipp shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead carrying 158 lb; the main risk is her inconsistency, having pulled up on two occasions in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who loves this trip (placed at 20-22f multiple times on good); Ciaran Murphy's yard is 2/15 in 14 days and the horse is fresh off 8 days, which carries some fitness risk but also suggests readiness — well-suited by a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Steps In The Sand arrives on the back of a second last time out, and third three starts back hints at consistency, though she remains yet to win in her last five starts; the 150 lb burden is a stern test for a mare rated 93 officially.

runners_data.name: Laurie Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 55 days for Delany; her recent form is moderate (one place from five runs on good) and the long absence combined with a big field makes a clean passage from the rear an optimistic expectation.
runners_data.comment: Laurie Blue returns after 55 days off carrying 149 lb, and her experience on today's going is a genuine asset for a mare our rating marks as the fourth-best of 18 here; the worry is a patchy recent spell that includes two pulled-up efforts, leaving her yet to score in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Prominent type with one win in 20f on good ground but Ryan's yard is 0/18 in 14 days, which is a stark stat; has finished no better than fifth in last four runs, making it hard to make a strong case despite suitable style.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, Andyourbirdcansing heads here on the back of an unplaced effort, and her record of one win in her last five starts offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 28-day break.

runners_data.name: Bowgate Street
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose true rear-of-field style is squeezed into midfield by the sheer volume of closers in this race; Flannery's yard is 0/3 in 14 days and a style-fit score of 0.94 means discounting this at a short price if racing out of role.
runners_data.comment: Bowgate Street shaped well enough with a third last time out, and a second three starts back gives her an obvious place claim, though a subsequent seventh and a long losing run in recent starts suggest inconsistency remains the worry under 148 lb.

runners_data.name: Evelyn
runners_data.note: True hold-up mare for Julie Cashin who has not won on good going in five attempts on similar ground; the 55-day layoff and a 0.93 style-fit flag — meaning she is unlikely to achieve her natural back-of-the-field position — are both reasons for caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up two runs back, Evelyn heads here 55 days on, carrying 148 lb; she has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 93 offers mild encouragement, though she faces a stiff task from a midfield ranking of ten of eighteen.

runners_data.name: Last Note
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type away for 90 days (longest absence in the field), trained by Cian Collins who is 0/15 in 14 days; the style-fit score of 0.92 signals she won't easily find her natural position, and her form string shows no wins on good ground in eight runs.
runners_data.comment: Last Note has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 104 against an official mark of 89, she carries the profile of a live threat — yet winless in her last five starts and returning after 90 days off, a return to form is the key question under 146 lb.

runners_data.name: Circus Act
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a 0.92 style-fit score mapped into midfield; best recent form has come on softer ground (fourth on soft/yielding) and her good-ground record over the distance is unconvincing — likely to be frustrated by traffic in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and stepping out after 41 days off, Circus Act does have experience over today's trip and going to call upon, though a tendency to find little in recent runs — and a 145 lb burden — makes progress hard to predict.

runners_data.name: Chemdawg
runners_data.note: Has placed at 1/19f on good ground (win) and has multiple placed efforts, making her arguably the most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses; McKiernan's yard is 0/2 in 14 days but the horse's form figures include two seconds and a win, so the ability is there if she can find clear air.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the field on our figures and clearly hard to fancy, though Chemdawg does bring distance and going experience to the table, and her second two starts back shows she can hit the frame; the 5th last time out, however, does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Rothwell's yard is 4/21 in 14 days (strong strike rate) and the mare has two wins at 20f on good and soft; a 0.91 style-fit score suggests she won't get her preferred hold-up berth, but the trainer form and course-distance profile make her one of the more interesting redistributed runners.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins three and four starts back give Larkins Lane some profile, but she has finished fourth and eighth in her two runs since, and ranked last of 18 on our figures, she faces a stiff task under 142 lb despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Demanding Gerry
runners_data.note: Multiple placed efforts at 17-20f on good ground for James Andrew Fahey, but no wins on good going and a 0.93 style-fit flag; racing out of natural role in this big field will make it hard to produce her best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, Demanding Gerry is hard to fancy, her most recent outing ending in a pulled-up, though she has placed twice in recent starts and does have experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a consistent fade-in-finish flag and no wins across 11 runs on similar going; the style-fit score of 0.93 and a form string of 0-0866 combine to make this a very difficult proposition in a 18-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Frontier Rose faces a stiff task, though she has experience of today's going and returns after a 28-day break fresh enough to improve.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: Away for 337 days — by far the longest absence in the field — and her last five runs show nothing above fourth; a 0.91 style-fit score and the fade-in-finish flag make her very hard to support on return.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last four starts and returning from a 337-day absence, St Anthonys Corner faces a stiff ask under 140 lb, though she has run over today's trip and conditions before and our rating of 90 suggests she retains some ability.

races.paceDynamic: Tir Og and Ivana D'alco are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over 2m3f on good ground at Kilbeggan, creating a genuine, honest gallop that is unlikely to relent. With Steps In The Sand and Andyourbirdcansing also pressing from prominent positions, the tempo will be sustained rather than tactical, putting a premium on stamina and jumping accuracy rather than a late turn of foot. The large 18-runner field means traffic and positioning will be a significant factor for those coming from off the pace, and the honest fractions set by two genuine front-runners are likely to stretch the field early on this galloping track. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently in the slipstream of the pace without being consumed by it — particularly those with proven good-ground form at this distance who can pick up when the leaders tire after the last. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Bowgate Street, Evelyn, Last Note, Circus Act, Chemdawg, Larkins Lane, Demanding Gerry, Frontier Rose and St Anthonys Corner — are true hold-up types pushed into midfield on the map because the field holds far more rear-of-the-field horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back; of these, Bowgate Street and Chemdawg are perhaps best-placed to find a forward position given their recent placed form, but none can be guaranteed their natural ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the front two set a genuine gallop that burns off hold-up horses and a prominent racer sweeps through late.
scenarios.body: Tir Og and Ivana D'alco establish a true pace over the 2m3f trip, thinning the field entering the home straight; horses traveling prominently without leading — Steps In The Sand, Diamond Tipp — are ideally positioned to mow down the tiring leaders after the last flight. This scenario rewards stamina, clean jumping and a prominent racing style on ground that is riding consistently good throughout the card.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders — most likely Ivana D'alco — dictates a controlled gallop and outstays all challengers to the line.
scenarios.body: Ivana D'alco, the Mullins-trained runner with Brian Hayes aboard, is capable of rating the gallop from the front and her good-ground form figures (1-6 in her only two runs on similar ground) suggest she handles this surface well enough to sustain her effort; if Tir Og wilts or makes a jumping error, Ivana D'alco can steal a decisive advantage. Tir Og also holds live claims under this shape as the other confirmed front-runner, and could outstay rivals if the pace is less combustive than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace proves too hot and both leaders capitulate, allowing midfield horses to charge through.
scenarios.body: With two front-runners fighting for supremacy and a big field applying early pressure, the gallop could become genuinely injurious to those who set it, leaving late-finishing types to clean up — Small Bucks and Del Boys Diva both carry fades-in-finish warnings but are OR-rated high enough to capitalise on a truly run race if they find a cleaner run than their redistribution would imply. This shape is structurally possible but partially undermined by the fact that the majority of ostensible closers in this field are genuine hold-up horses squeezed into midfield by race shape, meaning clean passages late are far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Headgear Edge
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field creates a scrappy, stop-start contest with significant interference, favouring horses with tactical adaptability and headgear assistance.
scenarios.body: A field this size on a galloping hurdle track can produce bunching, fallers and blocked runs, particularly for those drawn wide or forced wide on bends; horses wearing headgear that sharpens their response to the whip and keeps them focussed — Ivana D'alco (hood), Del Boys Diva (tongue-tie), Diamond Tipp (tongue-tie/pad) — may gain an edge if chaos reigns. This is the least structured scenario and the hardest to predict, but the big field and redistributed hold-up runners make interference a live risk that cannot be entirely dismissed.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tir Og and Ivana D'alco in the opening quarter-mile — if both dig in for the lead and push the tempo hard, the race could be decided before the home straight as the field strings out and hold-up horses lose contact.

Shirzan is a four-year-old stepping up markedly in trip for the first time over hurdles; if she hits a wall in the final half-mile, she could impede runners coming from behind in a densely packed 18-runner field.

St Anthonys Corner returns after 337 days off — monitor her in the parade ring and early in the race for any signs of ring-rustiness or jumping errors that could cause interference in the chasing pack.

Larkins Lane is one to track in-running: Rothwell's 14-day strike rate is the strongest of any trainer represented, and if she can defy her redistribution and find a forward pitch despite her natural hold-up style, she becomes a live each-way contender.

Brian Hayes' booking for Ivana D'alco (Mullins yard) stands out as the highest-profile jockey-trainer combination in the race — watch her market move in the final 30 minutes before post time as an indicator of stable confidence.

races.name: SIS Supporting Irish Racing Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hey Sir
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has run six times over hurdles without winning; Simon Torrens' booking adds little, and the redistribution to midfield reflects a field stacked with closers meaning he is unlikely to find the gap-heavy race shape his style requires.

runners_data.name: Kingston Silver
runners_data.note: One run over hurdles shows a tendency to fade late, which is the last thing you want in a race where the pace is likely to be controlled and the premium is on travelling well; natural hold-up racer displaced into midfield by the volume of similar types, making his task harder rather than easier.

runners_data.name: Tell Me See
runners_data.note: Three runs on good ground without troubling the judge; a genuine hold-up horse whose form string of 9-85 shows no sign of getting competitive, and on a track where Kilbeggan's tight finish suits sharp actioners over stayers who come from off the pace.

runners_data.name: The Bossman About
runners_data.note: Complete unknown — no runs to assess, Carl Millar claiming 5lbs, and trainer Nigel Thomas Slevin sends out his first runner with no 14-day form to reference; style is entirely unclassified so this horse could slot anywhere.

runners_data.name: Through The Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three hurdle runs, all on differing ground types; Philip Donovan takes the ride for Kelly's yard which has been in good form (3/12 T14), and the step up to 2m3f from previous 2m trips looks an asset on a galloping circuit.

runners_data.name: Not In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Finished third on debut over 2m on good ground with a hood, showing some ability; a genuine hold-up type redistributed to midfield given the glut of similar runners, meaning his one placing-level effort may flatter his prospects here where he won't naturally get cover from the rear.

runners_data.name: Blue Trix
runners_data.note: Unraced under rules, trained by the powerful W P Mullins (4/26 T14) and ridden by Danny Mullins — the yard's unknown quantities regularly arrive fit and capable on debut; style completely unclassified so he could race anywhere, making him the biggest unknown in the field.

runners_data.name: Online Order
runners_data.note: Hood and tongue-tie wearer who has run three times without landing a blow, finishing no better than sixth; a true hold-up horse placed in midfield by the map due to the redistribution pressure, and 44 days off the track adds a small fitness query.

runners_data.name: Roll It Roisin
runners_data.note: Recent run 10 days ago over the same 2m3f at Kilbeggan (finished 7th on good) gives useful track and trip form but the course hasn't flattered her; tongue-tie fitted, hold-up style, and trainer Kelly runs two in this race suggesting a role-player rather than stable star.

runners_data.name: Tiffany Case
runners_data.note: Two hurdle runs on good ground, finishing 5th and 9th; a hold-up type whose form shows she stays in touch but doesn't quicken off a steady pace, and Sean Flanagan's booking is the main positive with trainer Connell's 0/2 in 14 days offering no confidence boost.

runners_data.name: Tutu Twist
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for De Bromhead, who saddles his most prominent runner in this race; 142 days off the track is a notable fitness flag but the yard targets horses fresh, and on good ground over this exact 2m3f trip she sets the entire race tempo — the race revolves around her jumping and lasting.

races.paceDynamic: Tutu Twist is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Through The Storm as a likely companion in the early stages, she should be able to dictate a measured, uncontested gallop over this 2m3f trip on good ground at Kilbeggan. The pace is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out early, meaning the race will likely remain compact through the middle stages before quickening from the second-last hurdle. This shape — a single dominant pace-setter setting a sustainable tempo — strongly favours prominent and mid-division horses who can travel smoothly and produce a clean jump at the last, rather than true hold-up finishers who depend on a strong pace to make late ground. The field contains significantly more hold-up horses than can realistically settle at the rear and deliver a finish: Online Order, Not In A Hurry, Kingston Silver, Hey Sir, and others are redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the horses most likely to actually secure prominent positions are Tutu Twist and Through The Storm, with Blue Trix and The Bossman About unknown quantities who could slot anywhere.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tutu Twist Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Tutu Twist dictates a measured gallop unchallenged and jumps fluently, setting a pace that rewards those racing prominently.
scenarios.body: Tutu Twist, fresh off a 142-day break for De Bromhead but proven on good ground and over the trip, bowls along in front and her rivals never get competitive from off the pace; the sustainable tempo means the winner comes from on or near the pace rather than from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tutu Twist's long absence tells in the final stages and a well-positioned chaser storms past at the last.
scenarios.body: Through The Storm or Blue Trix travels smoothly just behind the leader and hits the front on the run to the last, with the moderate pace having kept the field together and allowed a prominent type to strike at the optimum moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses turning for home and the field bunches, giving a midfield traveller a clear run through to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Not In A Hurry or Hey Sir, both well-handled hold-up types forced to race closer than ideal, find a gap from a compressed pack and pick off tired horses late; this relies on more pace than is evident and on their redistribution disadvantage being overcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Outsider Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart chaotically — a faller, a loose horse, or a notable market mover running green — creating a muddled finish.
scenarios.body: The Bossman About or Kingston Silver, unknown quantities with unraced or limited profiles, benefit from fortune and disorder rather than tactical excellence; this is the least likely scenario given the clear pace structure but cannot be fully ruled out in a wide-open maiden.

watchPoints.text: Tutu Twist's 142-day layoff is the single biggest pivot point in the race — if she blows up turning for home, the entire pace structure collapses and a prominent chaser like Through The Storm or Blue Trix inherits the race.

Blue Trix is completely unraced and trained by W P Mullins with Danny Mullins aboard — Mullins debutants at this level regularly trade at long prices and win, making this horse a wildcard that current form analysis cannot adequately assess.

The volume of redistributed hold-up horses (Hey Sir, Kingston Silver, Not In A Hurry, Online Order) means the midfield is likely to be congested and scrappy from an early stage — any bumping or traffic trouble between hurdles could eliminate several runners' chances simultaneously.

Through The Storm steps up in trip from 2m to 2m3f for the first time and has run on softer ground previously — watch for whether he travels comfortably in a prominent position over the extra distance on good going before committing to him as the main pace beneficiary.

The Bossman About is a complete unknown with no prior form — jockey Carl Millar claiming 5lbs could be significant in a level weights race, and any unusual market move for this runner in the final 30 minutes before post time should be treated as a serious live signal.

races.name: Clarke's Bar Mullingar Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kamino Bello
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator on OR 110; Alix Balfe's 7lb claim is an asset but 48 days off and five previous runs all outside the top four suggest consistency is an issue at this level; Good going is fine, 2m3f suits.
runners_data.comment: Kamino Bello has going experience to call on and returns after a 48-day freshener carrying 166 lb off an official mark of 110, yet winless in his last five starts and a pulled-up effort most recently makes it hard to see him overturning his recent slide in form.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a recent win and a second from two recent starts, both on Good; prominent style suits the expected race shape well, Paddy Cody's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive, and the trip is an upgrade on last time which he handled well.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win the start before last and shaped with promise when second prior to that, but a tame ninth last time out clouds his claims; has run over today's trip and going, though 162 lb is a stern ask for a horse ranked sixth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Jacko Star
runners_data.note: 211 days off the track is a significant concern for a horse that has never won or placed in five prior starts and wears headgear; hold-up style means he needs everything to fall right, and fitness is the primary question mark here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 211 days away, Jacko Star faces a stiff ask carrying 162 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 105 offers some encouragement in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Rockstown Girl
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 meaning she is racing out of her natural role — her record shows she can lead but her best form has come from off the pace; James Smith's 5lb claim helps, and her Good-ground form across 12-15 runs is solid, but she must be discounted in scenarios requiring anything other than pace-setting.
runners_data.comment: Rockstown Girl showed a nice mix of consistency and a win in her last five starts, with two thirds and a second among her recent finishes, though a sixth last time out after 65 days raises a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and 162 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse back after just 13 days with a U (unseated) on last run; Sean Flanagan is a high-quality jockey and the horse has shown ability in placed efforts on Good, but the quick turnaround and jumping query need watching.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained prominent racer returning just six days after last run, which is a fast turnaround even for a fit horse; consistent placed form on Good ground over 2m makes the step to 2m3f a question, but five places from 11 starts speaks to reliability.
runners_data.comment: Dairy Force has experience of today's trip and going but remains yet to win in recent starts, and a trainer strike-rate of just 1/41 over the past fortnight is a concern; third one start back and second on two occasions offer some encouragement, though a fall last time out and a hefty 160 lb test his resolve here.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two seconds and a second in last four, so in form; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is useful, wearing headgear (tp), and Good going suits well over 2m-2m2f — the 2m3f trip here is at the outer limit of his range.
runners_data.comment: Eye Contact has been placed twice in his last five starts, including a second two starts back, and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround having already experienced today's trip and conditions; winless in recent starts, but our rating of 114 marks him out as the one to beat in a field of 17.

runners_data.name: Butch Coolidge
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won over 2m4f on Good — the trip is his friend; Brian Hayes is a capable pilot for trainer David Harry Kelly who has been firing recently (3/12 in 14 days); 12 days between runs is fine, but last three runs have all been outside the places.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out checks the enthusiasm, though he showed his best when winning within his last five starts, and familiarity with today's going helps; at 158 lb he carries plenty of weight, and our rating of 103 leaves him with little margin.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Prominent type on a perfect 15/15 Going record on Good ground — a consistent yardstick; Caragh Monaghan's 7lb claim is a significant positive, the horse wears a tongue tie, and two seconds and a third from last four starts suggest he runs his race every time, just needs to find a bit extra.
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Doubt has placed twice in her last six starts — second three starts back, and third four starts back — yet she remains winless and was sixth last time out, twenty days ago; the experience over today's trip and going at least means she arrives on familiar terms.

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form reads poorly (P-09PF) with two falls/PUs in last four; wears a hood (b) and the historical form over this sort of trip on Good is modest; Darragh O'Keeffe is a top-class booking but the horse's current form trajectory is concerning.
runners_data.comment: Following Orders brings solid claims here, ranked second in the field on our ratings and with experience of today's trip and conditions, yet his recent string of falls and pull-ups makes jumping fluency the one thing connections need most from him.

runners_data.name: Premier Rogue
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style places him further back than the map shows — he has been sitting midfield by necessity in this crowded field; OR 99 looks fair on best form, but 95 days off and a run of 300-90 form figures don't inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Premier Rogue has been winless in his last five starts, with only a third place in his recent form offering any real encouragement, and a 95-day absence plus a trainer firing at just 4% recently are genuine concerns, though he has going experience and a rating of 104 to his name.

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a win and four places from 15 starts — solid and consistent on Good; Jordan Gainford is in good order for Cian Collins and the horse wears headgear (tp), which has coincided with his better efforts; one of the most likely to get a clean prominent position behind Rockstown Girl.
runners_data.comment: Blue Reed has placed twice in his last three starts, including a third last time out, but ranked 13 of 17 on our figures he faces a stiff ask under 152 lb, and a recent seventh blunts confidence despite distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Smackwater Jack
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old hold-up performer placed in heavy traffic conditions — his best work has come over 3m+ (1m wins and 4 places at 3m range) and the 2m3f trip here is shorter than ideal; his natural role is at the rear but redistribution places him midfield, where he may struggle to find the same late gear.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, Smackwater Jack makes this a tough pitch, though he does bring distance and going experience plus a second and third in recent starts to suggest he retains some ability when the mood takes him.

runners_data.name: Warmer Days Ahead
runners_data.note: A 144-day absence is the overriding concern here — Oliver McKiernan's seven-year-old has run only over 3m+ trips recently and is stepping back in trip; a genuine hold-up type running midfield by necessity, with a visor (tv) in the headgear, but the layoff and unknown fitness make him hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Warmer Days Ahead returns after 144 days off carrying 151 lb, which adds to his concerns; experience over today's trip and going offers some hope, but he looks to have plenty to prove here.

runners_data.name: Bobby Kirova
runners_data.note: A four-year-old on just three career starts — the least experienced horse in the race — and a natural hold-up type being shown in midfield because of field saturation; Good ground suits, but limited experience in a 17-runner competitive handicap is a big ask, and trainer Michael Butler has 0/2 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with two consecutive sixth-place finishes, Bobby Kirova faces a stiff task ranked 15 of 17 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going, and the third two starts back offers a sliver of hope, but 146 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Tribal
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up runner with no wins or places in four starts, wearing a hood (h); Norman Lee has had one winner from three recent runners, but the horse's form figures (0075) suggest he is still learning and this is a tough race for that process.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Tribal faces a stiff task here; 53 days off the track adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's going before and that familiarity offers at least a slender foothold.

runners_data.name: Tudorista
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a critical concern for a hold-up type that needs to land the killer blow late; trainer Edward Power has 0/1 in 14 days, and five runs without a win or better than fourth on the recent form string make this an unlikely winning vehicle in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 16 of 17 on our figures, Tudorista faces a stiff ask, with a pull-up and two unplaced efforts among her recent outings; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 27-day absence, offer slim positives.

races.paceDynamic: Rockstown Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m3f trip on Good ground — a pace that will neither burn off the field early nor produce a sprint finish. Imarajan, Dairy Force, Sea Of Doubt, Blue Reed and Following Orders will press into prominent positions just off her, creating a compact, organised early order that should keep the tempo honest but not punishing. With the gallop controlled and the going riding consistently Good throughout the card, horses travelling smoothly in a handy position — just off the pace with cover — are best placed to pounce at the final hurdle, giving the edge to prominent-to-midfield runners who do not need to make up excessive ground. Several runners carry REDISTRIBUTED tags — Premier Rogue, Smackwater Jack, Warmer Days Ahead, Bobby Kirova and Tribal are genuine hold-up types forced into a midfield mapping because the field is saturated with closers; of those, none are likely to secure a truly prominent berth, and Smackwater Jack's stamina profile at this trip makes him the most credible of the group to finish off a steady-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rockstown Girl Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Rockstown Girl gets an uncontested lead and controls a genuine but sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets an even tempo that suits horses travelling prominently without expending energy, allowing the field to settle into a rhythm and leaving a premium on jumping fluently and kicking from the last; prominent types with good form on Good ground have a significant edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Imarajan or Dairy Force push up aggressively early and force Rockstown Girl to increase the pace, creating a two-or-three way tussle for supremacy.
scenarios.body: A contested lead in a big field compresses the midfield and tightens margins, rewarding horses that sit just off the lead with cover and jump well at the last two hurdles; Imarajan's last-time-out win and Dairy Force's consistent placed form on Good ground make them the principal threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that closers get a true end-to-end gallop to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the early tempo to be stronger than the map suggests — possible in a 17-runner field with horses jostling for position — and Smackwater Jack's proven stamina over 3m-range trips and Cocovic's hold-up profile give them a finishing kick if the leaders empty; however, several closers are redistributed types not running in their natural role, limiting the probability of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big-Field Scrimmage Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes crowding, interference or a change of pace mid-race that fragments the field.
scenarios.body: A 17-runner handicap hurdle on a tight track like Kilbeggan invites traffic problems and positional battles, and any runner carried wide or caught in a pocket late faces a sharply reduced chance; horses with high cruising speed who sit wide and clean — Imarajan and Blue Reed — can avoid the worst of it, while badly placed closers suffer most.

watchPoints.text: Rockstown Girl is the pivot of the entire race — if she jumps slowly or is bustled for the lead in the first mile by Imarajan or Dairy Force, the tempo accelerates sharply and the entire shape flips from scenario A to B, dramatically altering which horses are in contention.

The 17-runner field on Kilbeggan's tight track creates a significant risk of crowding and interference at hurdles, particularly for hold-up horses like Cocovic and Butch Coolidge who must weave through traffic in the straight — any bump or check at the final hurdle ends their chance.

Following Orders carries a recent fall (F) on its form string and wears a hood; in a big-field hurdle at pace, an erratic jumper at the head of affairs or close to prominent runners presents a safety concern for those racing around it.

Smackwater Jack and Warmer Days Ahead are both redistributed true hold-up horses — if the pace is steady and the race compresses late, they may lack the natural position to challenge, but if they somehow get clear runs their class at this distance over similar ground should not be dismissed entirely.

The entire card has returned Good going with no deterioration across eight races — the ground is consistent and reliable, meaning no horse has a going advantage or disadvantage, and form on Good can be taken at face value throughout.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Flat Race

runners_data.name: Back In Favour
runners_data.comment: Back In Favour arrives here on the back of a third last time out and a win three starts back, showing she retains the ability to compete at this level, and her experience on today's going is a further plus; the weight burden of 165 lb is the key question.

runners_data.name: Ballito Beauty
runners_data.comment: Ballito Beauty shaped with some promise when second last time out, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a featherweight she is not — 165 lb is a stiff burden — and our rating ranks her sixth of eleven, making her hard to fancy at face value.

runners_data.name: Bambi Fever
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked seventh of eleven on our figures, Bambi Fever faces a stiff ask under 165 lb, though she has run over today's going before and the 42-day break at least gives connections time to have her tuned up.

runners_data.name: Bonnie Loch
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Bonnie Loch is yet to win in recent starts but remains open to improvement; last seen finishing seventh thirty-one days ago, she returns fresh enough to step forward under a welterweight burden of 165 lb.

runners_data.name: No Brainer
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, No Brainer is yet to win in her last four starts but returns quickly after just 13 days, and the burden of 165 lb will need managing as connections look to unlock her potential.

runners_data.name: Pamelaisbrass
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pamelaisbrass does bring distance and going experience to the table and her third last time out shows she can threaten the frame, though 165 lb is a stern ask against this field.

runners_data.name: Pat O's Rock
runners_data.comment: Pat O's Rock finished fourth on her latest start and, with going experience in her favour and a rating of 95 placing her second in the field, she looks a genuine threat; the concern is the weight burden of 165 lb on a mare yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Peat Sounds
runners_data.comment: Peat Sounds shaped with promise when third last time out, has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 85 puts her firmly in contention as a leading danger; the main risk is she remains yet to score.

runners_data.name: Tamara Jane
runners_data.comment: Ran a solid third two starts back before her recent fourth, and a winner three starts back, Tamara Jane has going experience to call on and her rating heads the field — 165 lb is the one query but she has the form to carry it.

runners_data.name: Hakuna Suala
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just one start, Hakuna Suala returns from a 179-day absence following a pull-up on her sole outing, and this lightly raced filly remains yet to win but carries obvious potential for better under her 163 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Velvet Ash
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just one run to her name, Velvet Ash was fourth last time out and returns here after a 96-day break, carrying 163 lb, with plenty still to learn yet to score.

races.name: Jim Ryan Racecourse Services (Pro/Am) Flat Race

runners_data.name: Hurricane Leaf
runners_data.comment: Hurricane Leaf is unexposed and open to improvement, returning after 82 days off carrying 168 lb; yet to win in his last three starts, his third last time out at least hints at ability worth watching as he steps out again.

runners_data.name: Ifuknowuknow
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to score in his last two starts, Ifuknowuknow returns from a 251-day absence carrying 168 lb, but with so little exposed form he remains one to watch as he builds fitness and experience.

runners_data.name: Rememberwhat
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Rememberwhat has shown enough in recent starts to remain of interest — second last time out is the pick of his form, and he steps up here carrying 168 lb yet to win but with more likely in the locker.

runners_data.name: S T Hamo
runners_data.comment: Shaped with promise when third last time out, and S T Hamo arrives here fresh enough after 31 days off, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; winless in his last four starts, but our rating has him joint-top of this field.

runners_data.name: Two Pints Pat
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Two Pints Pat has everything to prove first time out carrying 168 lb, yet with no form to weigh up he remains an intriguing unknown who could be anything.

runners_data.name: Call My Name
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, Call My Name arrives on a 20-day break with going experience in his favour and behind a trainer firing at 28% in the last fortnight — the weight of 166 lb is the factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Fleurocco
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Fleurocco returns after 166 days off yet to score, but with just the one start on record he remains a gelding with plenty to discover, carrying 166 lb on his comeback.

runners_data.name: Walkwithmyfriend
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Walkwithmyfriend returns after 155 days off yet to win in recent starts, but with just one run on the book he remains a gelding with plenty still to discover, carrying 166 lb on his comeback.

runners_data.name: Killeedy
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last start, Killeedy nonetheless shapes as a strong threat off 48 days' absence, with experience of today's going and a rating of 97 that ranks her second in the field; the main risk is that weight of 161 lb places a stiff burden on her.

runners_data.name: Myluckymaker
runners_data.comment: Myluckymaker has finished second in each of her last two starts and shaped with plenty of promise over today's going, making her a strong threat here despite carrying 161 lb; the main risk is that she remains winless in recent starts and may find one too good again.
